title: Edge fallback economics playbook and scouting instrumentation
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Objective: Produce a pragmatic playbook and the instrumentation primitives required to detect, triage, and act on model fallback events originating in edge/APAC regions where latency and capacity constraints force model substitution.

Why this matters: Customers running RAG and low-latency chat at the edge are sensitive to tail-latency spikes and model availability. We lack systematic telemetry tying fallback triggers to procurement signals (e.g., model availability, cost delta, region saturation). Without that, teams react ad hoc and customers see inconsistent behavior and pricing surprises.

Scope:
- Define economic thresholds and heuristics that should trigger a fallback (cost-per-token delta, avg-queue-depth, KV cache hit skew by region).
- Instrument the Console and runtime tracing to capture the minimal event stream for fallback analysis: request context, chosen routing policy, chosen model variant, effective latency, per-token cost estimate, autoscale state.
- Build a lightweight scout pipeline that samples production traffic to evaluate candidate fallback variants (quantized vs full-precision, distillations) for quality regression risk.
- Deliver a prototype dashboard with three views: real-time fallback heatmap, cost-impact simulator, and model-variant scoring from scout runs.
- Produce the playbook with runbooks for on-call, PM decisions (convert to reserved capacity, increase burst, or widen fallback family), and procurement triggers for dedicated capacity.

Success metrics (90-day):
- Detect and tag >=95% of fallback events in the instrumented regions.
- Reduce customer-observed 99p latency regressions due to fallback by 30% via fast routing changes or capacity add.
- Provide procurement signal that reduces emergency reserved capacity purchases by showing simulated cost-benefit for 3 customers.

Deliverables:
- Instrumentation spec (artifact link below) and event schema.
- Scout pipeline prototype (ingest + A/B quality scorer).
- Console dashboard prototype + cost simulator.
- Playbook PDF and decision matrix for procurement and routing policy changes.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Telemetry fidelity vs token-cost accounting: collecting per-token charge with high fidelity increases runtime overhead; we propose periodic sampling + prefix/KV cache-aware heuristics to approximate cost impact.
- Scout sampling rate: high sampling gives better model quality estimates but increases traffic to candidate variants and could affect customer budgets; default to 0.5% sample with escalation knobs.
- Immediate fallback vs warm-starting variants: warm-start reduces quality regressions but increases memory footprint; recommend hybrid: keep a small warm pool for top-2 fallback families in each region.

Risks:
- Scout results may overfit to sampled queries if sampling bias is not addressed.
- Instrumentation gaps for legacy customers on older SDKs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Instrumentation is deployed in staging and captures a synthetic fallback test sequence reliably.
- Dashboard renders fallback heatmap for at least two APAC regions with live data.
- Playbook approved by Security & Reliability leads.
